open_points.subject: Kernel over-class read refusal and rollback
open_points.text: Kernel's permitted read whose answer would carry a personal-data value is refused whole as above its class: no field of the answer is disclosed, and a change it made is undone.
open_points.question: Which permitted Kernel read, admissible answer field, and state change instantiate this test, given that every currently permitted Kernel read is declared business_confidential and reads otherwise make no stated change?
options: Name an actual conditionally personal field of a permitted Kernel read and the change that must be rolled back.
State that this is a fault-injection test of the response-class gate and specify that every change in the call's transaction must be rolled back.
Remove the rollback clause and test only that an injected over-class answer is wholly withheld.
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as fault injection at the response-class gate and require rollback of the entire call transaction.

open_points.subject: scope of rollback after an over-class answer
open_points.text: a change it made is undone
open_points.question: What counts as a change that must be undone: only writes made by the operation, every durable effect including audit and sequence changes, or also runtime effects outside the store?
options: Undo every durable and runtime effect caused by the call.
Undo the whole store transaction, including audit entries and audit-sequence movement, but not unrelated runtime bookkeeping.
Undo only the record mutation performed by the operation.
open_points.default_guess: Undo the entire store transaction, including audit and audit-sequence effects, and leave no product-visible effect of the refused call.

open_points.subject: registration under the access-version increment invariant
open_points.text: accepted change of x other than its end => version(x)' = version(x) + 1
open_points.question: Does “accepted change of x” include initial registration, even though A12 rule 1 separately says the version is 1 at registration and no prior version(x) exists?
options: Exclude registration explicitly; registration creates version 1 and later accepted changes increment it.
Treat the absent pre-registration version as 0 and apply the invariant to registration.
Limit the invariant to accepted actions on an already registered session.
open_points.default_guess: Limit the invariant to an already registered session and state separately that registration creates version 1.

open_points.subject: listener state after a failed start check
open_points.text: Each start check that fails — a configuration item, a backup location that cannot be written, an existing store failing its integrity check or of another version, a new store that cannot be made — stops the start with no listener opened and no request served.
open_points.question: Does “no listener opened” mean that no listener was ever opened during the attempt, or only that no listener remains open when the failed start returns?
options: No listener may be opened until every other start check, including both bind checks, is known to succeed.
Listeners may be opened in the stated order, but every listener already opened must be closed before a failed start returns.
The phrase applies only to the listed pre-listener failures and must say so explicitly.
open_points.default_guess: For the listed pre-listener failures, no listener is ever opened; for a listener-opening failure, previously opened listeners are closed and none remains open.

witness.initial: All configuration, backup and store checks pass; the owner-interface endpoint is free, but the service-API endpoint cannot be bound.
events: Registry starts and reaches the listener checks.
Under A17 rule 2 it opens the owner-interface listener first.
Opening the service-API listener fails, so Registry closes the owner-interface listener and stops.
outcomes: A17 rule 2 permits the owner-interface listener to have been opened temporarily before it is closed.
Required test 10, read as covering every start check literally, requires that no listener was opened.
witness.observer: A bind observer or start test can observe whether the owner-interface socket was opened during the attempt.

open_points.subject: security review status after the current decision changes
open_points.question: Has the security review been performed again after the listed changes to A01, A02, A04, A09, A10, A11, A12, A14 and A17, as A21 rule 2 requires, or is it currently reopened?
options: Mark the review reopened until every affected category is reviewed, then add the new performed-again record.
Add a performed-again record for this change set and state the reviewed categories and outcomes.
Show that none of the changed decisions is named by a category; the present text does not support this option.
open_points.default_guess: Mark it reopened, review every category that references a changed decision, and only then restore PERFORMED.

witness.initial: A21 is marked PERFORMED and its categories reference A01, A02, A04, A09, A10, A11, A12, A14 and A17.
events: The current round changes those referenced decisions.
A21 rule 2 says that a change to a decision a category names reopens the review.
No performed-again passage for the current changes is present.
outcomes: Applying A21 rule 2 leaves the security review reopened.
Applying the displayed status treats the security review as already performed and complete.
witness.observer: The State 2 reviewer and gate see different review status for the same change set.

set_aside.subject: registration checks versus the A10 decision statement
set_aside.text: Accepted decision A10 — every agent-authority call is checked three times by Registry
set_aside.question: Must registering a new agent session receive only the Kernel-token check, or must it satisfy the decision title's three checks?
options: Change the decision statement to exempt registration and require only the token check for it.
Require registration to pass the session-registration check too, which prevents registering a new identity.
Define a different explicit set of three checks for registration.
set_aside.default_guess: Change the decision statement to say that every agent-authority call other than registration receives the applicable session and project checks; registration receives only the Kernel-token check.

witness.initial: Session identity x is not registered, and Cabinet Kernel presents its valid service token.
events: Cabinet Kernel calls 'register an agent session' naming x.
outcomes: The decision statement is applied literally: the call must receive all three checks and is refused because x is not registered.
A10 rule 1 and Required test 5 are applied: only the token is checked and x is registered.
witness.observer: Cabinet Kernel sees either an accepted new session or a refusal.
